headline: Huawei and Qualcomm announced a multi-year patent cross-licensing deal in 5G and AI, with Qualcomm also buying some Huawei US patents.
score_reason: Announced by the companies and widely reported; terms undisclosed and approval pending, so score kept at the pool level.
importance_line: Two of the biggest names in mobile chips now trade patent rights in both directions, which touches Huawei and Qualcomm licensing income and will face U.S. regulatory review, but the price and the net balance are not disclosed.
summary: Nikkei Asia reports that Huawei announced on Monday 5 Oct 2026 a cross-licensing agreement under which Qualcomm would pay to use Huawei patents in 5G and AI for the first time, making Qualcomm the net payer, while Huawei first paid Qualcomm for patents in 2001. Other outlets add that Qualcomm will also buy selected Huawei US patents; the deal needs regulatory approval, and its value and timing have not been disclosed.
notes: Source credit: Nikkei Asia (own reporting on the net-payer point). Nikkei page was paywalled after the first paragraph; supporting detail from tbreak.com. Net payer is Nikkei's reading, not a figure from the companies.
